title: Sentiment Bundle Benchmark
why: GURA's numbers came from validation sets that mixed in the test split, so the question of how to classify sentiment today needed a fair rerun. Spoiler: half a minute of TF-IDF on a CPU beats GURA's best IMDB claim.
gains: Before choosing a sentiment model, see what each option costs as well as what it scores: accuracy and macro-F1 next to training time, speed, VRAM and size, on identical splits. The best frozen embedding lands within two points of fine-tuning, so the budget gets a vote too.
lessons: Re-running ModernBERT on IMDB with the same seed moved macro-F1 from 91.6 to 90.9, so gaps under a point between fine-tuned models are noise.
Zero-shot, the 2B LLM called 98% of SUBJ sentences 'subjective'; eight examples in the prompt fixed that but hurt MR and MyAnimeList.
Re-reading the 2023 bundle found half the IMDB training set was generated word salad and the MyAnimeList scores slid out of line with their text.
subtitle: Compare sentiment models on the same terms
description: TF-IDF, embeddings, fine-tuned encoders and a local language model, evaluated on fixed splits across six sentiment datasets. The successor to GURA.
longDescription: A reproducible sentiment-classification benchmark across MyAnimeList reviews and five classic English datasets. Fixed splits and seeds support comparisons of accuracy, macro-F1, training time, inference speed, memory and model size. It replaces the older GURA BiGRU experiment.
features: Six datasets with fixed splits and seeds
TF-IDF, embeddings, ModernBERT, DeBERTa-v3 and local-model baselines
Accuracy, macro-F1, runtime, memory and model-size reports
Dataset bundle available on Hugging Face
